sentences.text: Arechia holds the distinction of being the oldest known genus of stingaree.
Fossil evidence suggests this ancient fish lived in warm, shallow waters similar to those inhabited by modern stingarees today.
The genus was formally described by Cappetta in 1983.
The species A. arambourgi honors Camille Arambourg, who first identified the teeth as Raja praealba in 1952.
Cappetta later separated males from females, placing the latter in the genus Merabatis.
Isolated teeth have been discovered in Senegal, Tunisia, and possibly Egypt.
This creature dwelt in the northern Tethys Ocean during the Early Eocene.
Its existence spanned a period between 59.24 and 37.71 million years ago.
Some researchers suggest isolated teeth may date as late as the Early Oligocene, though this remains unconfirmed.
